ctx.x: He had a great thing that I used to sit in. I took some classes with him called “Music for People,” about just teaching groups of people from a concert violinist to someone who never did music in their lives, to making good music together. And it was brilliant. And he invited me to come to this thing he did, it was in ’86, like a week-long thing in the summer where I would just hang out and be part of it. And so I grew, both fields started coming together, seeing how you could help teach someone. And the first…

and this idea flashes in my head to have him just walking through cheese. Because I was thinking about this thing. There’s a resistance. You know when you play music, like to learn jazz violin you really have to learn about what it’s like to play a horn. Because things come too easy. You know people that can play really well, you know it’s harder to learn to swing. And I think about like Ellington’s band, they could really lay back, but the rhythm section stayed right there — the difference between that and a…
